decisive_items: worsened after waking and improved after lying down
response.rationale: Ptosis and diplopia with diurnal variation and negative edrophonium/antibody tests still best fit myasthenia gravis; third nerve palsy is contradicted by normal pupils and full extraocular movements.

rejected.why: Trauma history is nonspecific and does not explain the ocular pattern.
Normal pupillary reflexes and no extraocular movement limitation argue against third nerve palsy.
Superior orbital fissure syndrome would involve more cranial nerve deficits and pupillary changes.
Adie syndrome requires pupillary abnormality, which is explicitly absent.
